{"findings":[{"rule_id":"MF-005","evidence":[{"kind":"title_block","ref":"heat_treatment","page":1,"quote":"---"},{"kind":"note","ref":"N3","page":1,"quote":"1) TO BE CASE HARDENED UPTO 55~60 HRC.
2) CASE DEPTH 0.8~1.2mm.
3) THREADS TO BE KEEP SOFT.
4) RETAPPING TO BE DONE AFTER SURFACE TREATMENT AT SUPPLIER END.( IF APPLICABLE )"}],"comment":"The title-block heat_treatment field is '---' while note N3 specifies case hardening to 55–60 HRC with a 0.8–1.2 mm case depth, but neither states at which manufacturing stage the treatment applies (e.g., after rough machining, before final grinding). Without the stage, the shop cannot sequence operations correctly, risking distortion of finished features or inability to hold tolerances. Update the heat_treatment field or note N3 to state when in the process route the case hardening is performed.","recommended_correction":"Add the manufacturing stage for the case hardening in the title block or in note N3 (for example, 'after rough machining, before finish grinding')."},{"rule_id":"WPM-003","evidence":[{"kind":"note","ref":"N3","page":1,"quote":"1) TO BE CASE HARDENED UPTO 55~60 HRC.
2) CASE DEPTH 0.8~1.2mm.
3) THREADS TO BE KEEP SOFT.
4) RETAPPING TO BE DONE AFTER SURFACE TREATMENT AT SUPPLIER END.( IF APPLICABLE )"}],"comment":"Note N3 calls out case hardening and explicitly keeps the threads soft, but no area on the drawing is marked with XXXXX to show where the hardened zone begins and ends. The heat treater has no visual boundary to follow, so the transition between hard case and soft thread root may fall in the wrong location, weakening the stud or making the threads un-tappable. Add XXXXX hatching or a dimensioned boundary on the view to define the case-hardened area.","recommended_correction":"Mark the area to be case hardened with XXXXX on the drawing views, clearly showing the boundary relative to the thread (F1 / D11)."},{"rule_id":"TL-014","evidence":[{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D5","page":1,"quote":"⌀ 22"},{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D8","page":1,"quote":"22"},{"kind":"title_block","ref":"title","page":1,"quote":"CYL MTG STUD R01"}],"comment":"The part is a cylindrical mounting stud (per the title block), yet the ⌀22 diameter (D5, D8) carries no runout or concentricity control relative to a datum axis. A mounting stud that is not controlled for runout can wobble or misalign the mounted cylinder, causing vibration or uneven wear. Add a runout tolerance on the cylindrical features referencing the appropriate bearing or locating axis.","recommended_correction":"Apply a circular or total runout GD&T callout on the ⌀22 feature (D5/D8) relative to the stud's functional datum axis."}]}
